content.title: About
content.content: Chili with macaroni is a hearty dish that combines a spicy meat chili sauce with tender pasta. It is popular in the US and Russia as a quick, satisfying meal for lunch or dinner.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish originated in the mid‑20th century in American cafeterias where macaroni was used as an inexpensive side.
Spiciness can be adjusted by varying the amount of chili peppers, paprika, and spices, making it suitable for any palate.
Variations include adding beans, corn, cheese, or sour cream.
Chili with macaroni is often served in a single‑pot “casserole” style for camping or quick home cooking.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: The meat in chili provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue repair.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Beef and red peppers contain iron that supports normal blood formation.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Spices and meat are good sources of vitamins B6 and B12, important for metabolism.

items.title: Fiber from pasta
items.content: Whole‑grain macaroni adds dietary fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: Antioxidants from spices
items.content: Capsaicin in chili peppers has antioxidant and anti‑inflammatory properties.

items.title: Spiciness
items.content: Very hot chili can irritate the stomach of people with sensitive digestion.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Prepared chili sauces often contain a lot of salt; monitor the amount used.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Traditional pasta contains gluten; gluten‑free alternatives are needed for celiac disease.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The dish can be calorie‑rich due to meat and cheese; portion control is advised for weight management.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot, optionally topped with grated cheese, fresh herbs, or sour cream. You can add avocado or a squeeze of lime for brightness. It is eaten with a spoon or fork.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool to room temperature, then store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Reheat on the stove or in a microwave, adding a splash of water to keep it moist.
